scope: High-priority hemp/Cannabis evidence for seedling damping-off biology, differential diagnosis, and prevention.
rules: Damping-off is treated as a syndrome with multiple possible causal organisms.
Visual symptoms do not provide species-level confirmation.
Prevention claims are separated from pesticide legality, label authorization, and organism-specific efficacy.
All mappings remain pending independent science review.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Hemp/Cannabis damping-off can involve multiple oomycete or fungal agents and may occur before or after emergence; prevention therefore emphasizes sanitation, drainage, clean propagation inputs, environmental management and scouting while causal identification requires evidence beyond visual collapse alone.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Ocamb, PNW Plant Disease Management Handbook, Hemp - Damping-off; Punja (2021), PMID 33427362, DOI 10.1002/ps.6307.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's syndrome framing, pre/post-emergence distinction and layered prevention/diagnostic workflow.
claimEvidence.limitations: Symptoms are not species-level confirmation. Pathogen prevalence, temperature response, product efficacy and pesticide legality vary by organism, production system and jurisdiction.
